newsitem.title: UK: Gold consumption falls in 1996 4th qtr - WGC.
newsitem.headline: Gold consumption falls in 1996 4th qtr - WGC.

text.p: Gold consumption in the fourth quarter of 1996 fell to 698.5 tonnes versus 716.3 tonnes in the same period of 1995, according to World Gold Council figures released on Wednesday.
But demand in the final quarter of 1996 was about 50 tonnes higher than in the third quarter of the year.
Gold demand in the emerging countries rose 3.0 percent to 456.3 tonnes aided by a 17 percent rise in India.

Demand in Western industrial nations fell 11 percent to 242.20 tonnes owing to lower interest in buying gold as an investment, the WGC said. The WGC monitors gold demand in countries accounting for about 75 percent of total world consumption.

George Milling-Stanley, manager of the WGC statistics division, said the fall in investment demand was not indicative of a long-term trend as 1995's high investment offtake was "a logical response to bizarre movements in exchange rates." - London Newsroom +44 171 542 7729
